title: Approach2: run Neo4j docker import + verify
description: Docker daemon must be running; then run ./approach2-using-existing-graph/scripts/neo4j_up_and_import.sh and verify data in Neo4j Browser (http://localhost:7474).
notes: Ports aligned to 7474/7687 in helper script

title: Feature: Deterministic risk report from user-provided Azure resource identity (no Terraform plan)
description:
Replace Terraform plan-driven workflows with a user-driven workflow where the user specifies the Azure resource being changed (resource ID and/or name+type+scope). The system resolves that input to a single graph entity in Neo4j, gathers bounded/allowlisted evidence, applies deterministic scoring rules, and outputs a reproducible risk report.

Scope:
- Inputs: Azure Resource ID OR (name + resource type + subscription + resource group) with interactive disambiguation.
- Entity resolution: deterministic, explicit tie-breakers, and clear errors.
- Evidence: only from allowlisted Cypher templates with strict bounds (limits/timeouts/max-hop/max-results) and no user-supplied Cypher.
- Output: deterministic ordering and stable report format.

Non-goals:
- Terraform plan parsing/integration.
- Auto-discovery of “what changed” beyond the provided resource identity.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLI accepts user-provided resource identity and produces a risk report for that entity.
- Same inputs against same DB snapshot yield identical score and evidence ordering.
- Neo4j access is via allowlisted, bounded queries only; no arbitrary Cypher execution.
- Clear UX for invalid/ambiguous inputs, with non-interactive mode support.

title: Deterministic Graph-Based IaC Risk Scoring (Neo4j Approach 2 MVP)
description:
Build an auditable, deterministic risk scoring workflow for changes where the user provides the resource being changed (no Terraform plan integration). The system uses (1) a canonical change model, (2) bounded/allowlisted Neo4j evidence queries, and (3) a versioned rules-based scoring formula.

Outputs must include: score, level, factors, evidence, unknowns, and risk_model_version. LLMs (if used) may explain but must not influence scoring.

Context: temp-risk-approach.md and approach2-using-existing-graph/README.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic output for identical inputs and unchanged graph
- Evidence collection is allowlisted + bounded (depth/limits) and read-only
- Output schema is stable + versioned; includes unknowns/confidence signals
- Docs show end-to-end usage on the sample Neo4j dataset

title: Golden/regression harness for scoring stability
description:
Add an automated harness that runs golden cases and asserts exact score/factors/evidence ordering stability for scoring model v1.

Goal: prevent unintended drift and make changes explicit via version bumps.
acceptance_criteria:
- One command runs golden cases and fails on any drift (score/factors/order)
- Golden outputs are tied to risk_model_version
- Failures clearly show which factor/output changed

title: Deterministic scoring rules: compute risk score from bounded evidence
description:
Implement the scoring engine as deterministic, rule-based evaluation over evidence gathered for the resolved entity.

Requirements:
- Fixed rule set and weights (config-driven is OK if pinned/versioned).
- Stable ordering of rules and findings.
- Score is reproducible given same evidence.
- Explicit handling for missing evidence (no silent fallbacks).

Output should be a structured intermediate form (e.g., `ScoreResult`) that the reporter formats.
acceptance_criteria:
- Given the same evidence input, produces identical score + rule findings ordering.
- Rules are bounded (no extra DB queries outside evidence layer).
- Missing evidence produces explicit “unknown/not-applicable” outcomes (deterministic).

title: CLI: accept Azure resource identity via flags + interactive prompts
description:
Define the user input contract for identifying the resource being changed. Support:
- `--resource-id` (preferred)
- Or `--resource-name`, `--resource-type`, `--subscription-id`, `--resource-group`
- `--non-interactive` mode (fail fast on missing/ambiguous)
- Interactive prompts when required fields are missing or ambiguity exists.

Deliver a single canonical “ResourceSpec” structure for downstream steps.
acceptance_criteria:
- Running the CLI with `--resource-id` proceeds without prompts.
- Running without required fields triggers prompts in interactive mode and errors in `--non-interactive`.
- A canonical parsed `ResourceSpec` is produced with normalized casing and validated required fields.

title: Evidence extraction contract (typed evidence model + mappings)
description: Define the evidence schema consumed by the scorer and the mapping rules from each allowlisted query output into evidence fields, including how to represent missing data (unknowns).
acceptance_criteria:
- Evidence schema (fields + types + meaning) is defined
- For each allowlisted query: mapping rules to evidence fields are documented
- Unknowns semantics are explicit and deterministic

title: Risk scoring CLI (resource-based input)
description: Implement a CLI that accepts resource-based input + operation (per CIM), resolves the resource in the graph, runs allowlisted/bounded evidence queries, computes score via scoring model v1, and outputs deterministic JSON (including risk_model_version, factors, evidence, unknowns).
acceptance_criteria:
- CLI accepts resource input + operation and produces valid JSON output
- Uses only allowlisted evidence queries; rejects any non-allowlisted query execution
- Enforces bounded retrieval (limits/depth) and read-only evidence collection
- Output is deterministic for repeated runs against unchanged graph

title: UX hardening: clear errors, disambiguation prompts, and non-interactive behavior
description:
Polish the CLI UX around validation and resolution:
- Human-friendly errors with next-step guidance.
- Interactive disambiguation prompt UX (paged list, show key properties, copy/paste resource ID).
- `--non-interactive` strictly forbids prompts and returns actionable exit codes.
- Add `--dry-run` option to show resolved entity and evidence queries that would run (no score).
acceptance_criteria:
- Ambiguity path is fast and user-friendly in interactive mode.
- `--non-interactive` mode never prompts and exits with stable error codes.
- `--dry-run` prints resolved entity + allowlisted query IDs without running scoring.

title: CIM spec (v1): resource-provided change input
description:
Define Canonical Change Impact Model (CIM) v1 for proposed changes when the user provides the resource being changed.

Must include required fields (resource_ref, operation, environment) and optional metadata as needed for scoring/evidence lookup.
acceptance_criteria:
- CIM v1 defines required vs optional fields and semantics
- Includes at least 3 example payloads (e.g., AzureResource, Service, Subscription scoped)
- Examples are internally consistent and unambiguous for graph lookup

title: Input validation: parse/normalize Azure Resource ID and resource type
description:
Implement strict validation and normalization for Azure identifiers.

Key behaviors:
- Parse Azure Resource ID into components (subscription, resource group, provider namespace, type segments, name segments).
- Normalize resource type to canonical form (e.g., `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines`).
- Validate allowed characters/lengths; reject obviously invalid IDs early.
- Provide actionable error messages (what’s missing/invalid).

Note: This task is purely input-side; graph resolution happens separately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Valid Azure Resource IDs are parsed into structured components.
- Invalid IDs (missing segments, wrong prefix, illegal chars) are rejected with clear messages.
- Resource type normalization is deterministic and documented (examples covered).

title: Docs: update README with new workflow (resource identity input) and examples
description:
Update docs to remove Terraform plan references and describe the new workflow.

Include:
- CLI examples using `--resource-id` and using name/type/scope.
- Explanation of determinism constraints and evidence allowlist.
- Troubleshooting for ambiguous resolution.
- How to run Neo4j import (Approach2) and then run the scorer.
acceptance_criteria:
- README and approach docs describe the resource-identity workflow clearly.
- Terraform plan integration is not mentioned as required for scoring.
- Examples are copy/paste runnable against the sample Neo4j dataset.

title: Test coverage: validation, entity resolution, evidence allowlist/bounds, determinism
description:
Add tests focused on the safety and determinism constraints:
- Azure resource ID parsing/normalization test vectors.
- Entity resolution ambiguity handling (candidate ordering, selection behavior).
- Evidence layer allowlist enforcement + bounds (limit/depth/timeout) behavior.
- Snapshot-style determinism tests for report ordering.

Prefer unit tests with mocked Neo4j driver; add a small integration test only if the repo already supports it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests cover input validation + normalization edge cases.
- Evidence layer blocks arbitrary Cypher and enforces bounds.
- Determinism tests ensure stable outputs for fixed fixtures.
- CI/local test command documented.

title: Entity resolution: map ResourceSpec to a single Neo4j node deterministically
description:
Resolve the validated `ResourceSpec` to one graph entity (or a deterministic, user-guided selection).

Resolution strategy:
- Prefer exact match on full Azure Resource ID when available.
- If only (name+type+scope): query candidates within scope; if multiple matches, deterministically sort and (a) prompt user to choose in interactive mode, (b) error with candidate list in non-interactive mode.
- Emit a stable `ResolvedEntityRef` (node id + key properties) for downstream evidence gathering.

Include guardrails:
- Cap candidate result size; provide guidance to narrow scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- With a known resource ID present in DB, resolves to exactly one node.
- With ambiguous inputs, interactive mode prompts for selection; non-interactive mode exits with a deterministic candidate list.
- Candidate ordering is stable and documented.
- Resolution query is bounded (max results) and uses allowlisted templates.

title: Approach2: Deterministic agent-derived risk report
description: Implement deterministic risk scoring + structured Markdown reporting via the Risk Assessment agent using the Neo4j MCP server (no standalone CLI).
acceptance_criteria:
- Using the Risk Assessment agent + Neo4j MCP, assessing a Service/AzureResource/Subscription returns a single Markdown report
- Report includes: resolved entity table, evidence summary table, derived relationship map, score breakdown table, and top-N evidence tables
- Score is deterministic given the same graph state (stable sorting, integer rubric, no randomness, no time-based drift unless asked)
- Approach 2 README points to agent usage/prompt
close_reason: Aligned to agent+Neo4j MCP (structured Markdown + deterministic rubric) and removed standalone CLI.

title: Constrained explanation contract ("explain only what's computed")
description: Define a constrained explanation format so any generated narrative can only cite computed factors/evidence/unknowns (no new claims). Scoring remains deterministic and independent of any LLM.
acceptance_criteria:
- Contract specifies explanation may cite only computed factors/evidence/unknowns
- Includes at least 3 example explanations based on golden cases
- Unknowns/confidence handling is described

title: Report generation: stable markdown + optional JSON output including evidence
description:
Generate the final risk report with:
- Stable section ordering and deterministic sorting of evidence and findings.
- A concise summary (score, severity, top drivers).
- Evidence appendix referencing the allowlisted query IDs and returned rows.
- Optional `--format json` for automation.

Ensure no sensitive/raw DB internals leak beyond what’s needed (bounded fields).
acceptance_criteria:
- Markdown output is deterministic for same inputs.
- JSON output matches a documented schema and includes score + evidence references.
- Report includes enough detail to justify the score without unbounded dumps.

title: Deterministic scoring model v1 (rules + factor taxonomy + golden cases)
description:
Define scoring model v1 that consumes CIM + evidence and produces: score, level, factors (typed), unknowns, and risk_model_version.

Document determinism rules (ordering, tie-breaks, caps). Provide golden cases with expected outputs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scoring spec includes formula/weights/caps and factor taxonomy
- Determinism rules are explicit (ordering, tie-breaks, caps)
- At least 5 golden cases with exact expected outputs tied to risk_model_version

title: Approach 2 docs update: end-to-end scoring workflow
description: Update docs to cover: starting/importing Neo4j sample data, running the risk scoring CLI with a resource, interpreting JSON output, and constraints (allowlist, bounded retrieval, determinism).
acceptance_criteria:
- Docs show how to start/import Neo4j and validate import
- Docs show how to run the scoring CLI with a resource and what output fields mean
- Docs emphasize constraints: allowlisted queries, bounded retrieval, deterministic scoring

title: Neo4j evidence layer: allowlisted Cypher templates with strict bounds
description:
Create a small evidence-query abstraction that enforces:
- Only allowlisted query IDs (no raw Cypher).
- Parameter schema validation (types, max lengths).
- Hard limits: `LIMIT` caps, max-hop depth, max rows per query, timeouts.
- Stable ordering for returned evidence rows.

This layer should be the only code path that talks to Neo4j for risk scoring/evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- Attempting to run non-allowlisted queries is blocked.
- Each evidence query enforces bounds (limit, depth, timeout) and returns stable ordered results.
- Evidence results include minimal, safe fields needed for scoring/reporting.
- Unit tests cover allowlist enforcement and bounds.

title: Neo4j evidence query allowlist (bounded templates)
description:
Declare an allowlisted set of parameterized Cypher templates for evidence collection (e.g., entity context, blast radius <=2 hops, incident/outage history, deployments/change events where available).

All evidence collection must remain read-only and bounded by depth/limits.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each query has: name, parameters, max depth/limits, expected output fields
- All queries are read-only (MATCH/RETURN) and bounded (LIMIT + depth caps)
- Queries align with CIM/resource resolution identifiers

title: Risk Assessment Agent: structured markdown output
description: Update the Risk Assessment Agent instructions to require structured Markdown output (tables) and an explicit deterministic scoring rubric aligned with the CLI.
acceptance_criteria:
- Agent output format specifies Markdown sections and tables
- Sorting/formatting rules documented to reduce variability
- Scoring rubric defined as deterministic integer math with caps/thresholds
close_reason: Updated Risk Assessment Agent instructions for structured Markdown output and deterministic scoring/ordering rules.

title: Resource resolution + input validation (CIM → graph node)
description:
Define deterministic rules for resolving CIM.resource_ref to a unique graph node, including validation and error handling (not found / ambiguous / multiple matches).

Resolution must be bounded and read-only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Resolution rules are deterministic and documented
- Explicit error shapes for: not found, ambiguous, multiple matches
- Lookup queries are bounded (LIMIT) and read-only
